prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view of an open electrical control cabinet in front of and below the camera wearer (0.5–1.0 m away), with a coworker in an orange vest immediately to the right (0.2–0.7 m away) and the camera wearer's own left arm extending from the bottom-center (0.3–0.6 m away) to hold the open cabinet door on the left. In frames 1 and 2, the coworker's head and torso are very bright and close (about 0.2–0.4 m from the camera), facing down and to the left toward the cabinet interior rather than toward the camera wearer, while his right arm reaches into the deeper, darker recess of the cabinet (~0.8–1.0 m away, about 0.4 m from the camera wearer's hand). Across frames 3 to 5, the coworker retreats rightward and upward out of the immediate foreground (to roughly 0.5–0.8 m away, leaving only his torso and right hand in view), while the camera wearer's left hand pushes the cabinet door upward and to the right to close it, causing the door's upper-left corner to become bright as it swings closer (~0.3 m). The depth map clarifies the continuous 3D slant of the hinged door, the recessed depth of the cabinet box relative to the foreground arms, and the coworker's step back, which are harder to judge from the overhead RGB angle alone. However, the depth map looks unreliable in frames 1 and 2 where the dark shadow inside the cabinet makes the coworker's reaching hand and the internal wiring appear overly far and indistinct compared to frames 3–5, and it saturates to pure white on the coworker's head in frames 1–2.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground people on the right and bottom-center from the unlabelled background cabinet, structural pipes, and looped cables on the left, placing the coworker on the right at roughly 0.2–0.8 m from the camera wearer and about 0.2–0.5 m to the right of the camera wearer's outstretched left arm. Both the camera wearer and the coworker are within arm's reach of the electrical cabinet and its hinged door, with the coworker's lower body and back occluded by the right frame edge throughout and his head moving out of view above the top-right edge after frame 2 as he retreats rightward and turns slightly away. Across the 5 frames, the masks track the separation between the two people as the coworker pulls his right arm back from inside the cabinet (frames 1–3) to rest near his side (frames 4–5) while the camera wearer's left arm pivots the door upward and rightward. While the map makes the boundary between the camera wearer's arm and the coworker's body clearer in frames 2, 3, and 5 than a quick glance at the busy RGB background, it is highly unreliable across the sequence. Specifically, it merges the camera wearer's arm and the coworker into a single 'person' instance in frame 1, misclassifies the pipes and cables on the lower left as a 'bicycle' in frame 1, mislabels the coworker's orange vest as a 'suitcase' in frame 4, and misses the electrical cabinet and door entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only a single magenta left-hand skeleton belonging to the camera wearer in the lower-left to center-left region of the frame (roughly 0.5–0.6 m from the camera), gripping the bottom edge of the open cabinet door. Across frames 1 to 3, this hand remains at a nearly constant position below and to the left of the coworker's reaching right hand (separated by about 0.4 m), before disappearing in frame 4 and reappearing slightly higher and further right in frame 5 as the arm pushes the cabinet door toward the closed position. The map shows the precise finger flexion and wrist orientation of the camera wearer's left hand grasping the door flange, which is partially blended against the metallic edge and cables in the RGB image. However, the pose map is largely unreliable for scene-level spatial understanding because it completely fails to detect the camera wearer's left hand in frame 4, misses the coworker's right hand reaching into and retracting from the cabinet across all 5 frames, and fails to fit any yellow body skeletons due to the steep top-down egocentric viewpoint and heavy truncation of both bodies at the frame edges.
